record.paper_title: Notes on open questions within density functional theory (existence of a derivative of the Lieb functional in a restricted sense and non-interacting v-representability)
record.context_brief: Restricted bounded derivative of the Kohn-Sham potential
record.original_question: Does the Kohn-Sham potential functional vs[ns], defined for non-interacting ensemble v-representable densities ns in Bs, admit a derivative in a restricted sense for every ns in Bs, and is that derivative bounded? The notes identify a positive answer as sufficient to prove the non-interacting v-representability conjecture, but they also note that establishing such a derivative rigorously is difficult, especially in degenerate cases, and that the inverse response kernel χs^-1[vs[ns]] is unbounded.

evidence.quote: Theorem 4.2 (Non-interacting v-representability and derivative of the KS potential). If a derivative of vs[ns] exists in a restricted sense for ns ∈ Bs and if this derivative is bounded, then the non-interacting v-representability conjecture is true.
In the following, we give some static linear response-based elements that hopefully contribute to the reflection on the existence of some derivative of vs[ns].

However, as αj can become arbitrailly close to 0, 1/αj is not bounded. This implies that the representation of −χ−1 s [vs[ns]] in the orthonormal eigenvector basis is not bounded, so as its representations in any other basis. So, even if it was possible to rigorously demonstrate that χ−1 s [vs[ns]] represents a derivative of the KS potential in a restricted sense, the unboundedness of χ−1 s [vs[ns]] would not allow to conclude that the non-interacting v-representability conjecture is true

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Consider the Kohn–Sham (KS) framework of density functional theory in which one considers N-electron systems described by single-particle densities ρ on R^3 with ρ ≥ 0 and ∫ρ = N. A density n_s is said to be non-interacting (pure-state or ensemble) v-representable if there exists a one-body local potential v_s such that n_s arises as the ground-state density of a non-interacting N-electron Hamiltonian H_s = -½Δ + v_s (acting on a Slater determinant or an ensemble of degenerate ground-state determinants). Let B_s denote the set of non-interacting ensemble v-representable densities. By the Hohenberg–Kohn theorem applied to non-interacting systems, the assignment n_s ↦ v_s[n_s] is well defined (up to an additive constant) on B_s, giving the KS potential functional v_s : B_s → (potentials modulo constants).

Let χ_s[v_s[n_s]] denote the static non-interacting density–density linear response operator at the potential v_s[n_s], i.e. the operator giving δn_s in terms of an infinitesimal perturbation δv_s of the KS potential at fixed particle number; let χ_s^{-1}[v_s[n_s]] denote its (formal) inverse on the space of density variations summing to zero.

We say that v_s admits a "derivative in a restricted sense" at n_s ∈ B_s if there exists a linear operator D[n_s], acting on an admissible class of density variations δn (those tangent to B_s, i.e. preserving total particle number and remaining inside B_s to first order), such that
   v_s[n_s + δn] - v_s[n_s] = D[n_s] · δn + o(‖δn‖)
in a suitable norm, modulo additive constants. The operator D[n_s] is said to be bounded if it extends to a bounded linear operator on the relevant Banach space of density variations.

Question. Does the KS potential functional v_s : B_s → potentials admit, at every density n_s ∈ B_s (including degenerate ground-state cases), a derivative in the above restricted sense, and is this derivative bounded? Equivalently, can one rigorously establish such a bounded restricted derivative of v_s[n_s] on B_s, in a way that would imply the non-interacting v-representability conjecture (the statement that every "reasonable" N-electron density is non-interacting ensemble v-representable)?

Note that the natural candidate D[n_s] = -χ_s^{-1}[v_s[n_s]] is in general unbounded, since the eigenvalues α_j of χ_s can approach 0, so a separate argument or alternative construction is required.
artifact.status_search_result: The general non-interacting v-representability problem and the existence of a (bounded) derivative of the KS potential functional in a restricted sense remain open. Partial progress has been obtained in restricted settings: a 2025 work treats non-interacting Schrödinger operators with distributional potentials on the one-dimensional torus, showing Hohenberg–Kohn and that the non-interacting Lieb functional is differentiable on the v-representable densities in that setting. No general resolution of the conjecture (covering degenerate cases in R^3) appears in the literature.

status_evidence.title: v-representability and Hohenberg-Kohn theorem for non-interacting Schrödinger operators with distributional potentials in the one-dimensional torus
status_evidence.snippet: The non-interacting Lieb functional is differentiable at every point in the space of v-representable densities (in the 1D torus, distributional-potential setting).
status_evidence.claim: Differentiability of the non-interacting Lieb functional has been established only in a restricted setting, suggesting the general question remains open.

status_evidence.title: The Structure of Density-Potential Mapping. Part I: Standard Density-Functional Theory
status_evidence.snippet: The overlap between interacting and noninteracting v-representability is poorly understood, with direct implications for Kohn–Sham theory.
status_evidence.claim: v-representability remains poorly understood and is treated as an open foundational issue in DFT.

status_evidence.title: On the v-Representability Problem in Density Functional Theory: Application to Non-Interacting Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the non-interacting v-representability problem as an outstanding question.
status_evidence.claim: The non-interacting v-representability question is reported as still outstanding.
